dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: Our city wants to ban cars from the center. What do you think?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I think it is a bold idea, but it could reduce pollution and traffic significantly.

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: But what about people who depend on their cars, like delivery drivers?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: They could receive special permits, so the plan would not hurt local businesses.

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: Public transport would have to improve first. Our buses are rarely reliable.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Exactly. Without frequent and punctual services, the plan will fail.

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: And the fares are expensive for families with several children.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: A cheaper monthly pass would encourage more people to leave their cars at home.

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: Cars are so convenient, though. I can go anywhere whenever I want.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Convenient, yes, but you also lose time in traffic and spend a lot on parking.

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: That is true. I spend nearly an hour a day looking for a place to park.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Some cities show that cycling lanes can work very well.

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: Perhaps, but our winters are harsher than theirs.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Fair enough, which is why a mix of solutions is probably necessary.

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: I might support the plan if the trains and buses improve.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That would be the right condition. Change works best when people have alternatives.
